reproResult: Followed all five layers (A–E) in my own worktree (HEAD a108fa7ef, involved files identical to base 16ceb3a54; git log 16ceb3a54..origin/main touches none of them, so not fixed on main). A: waf-probe.sh reproduced verbatim — /backend-api/transcribe returns HTTP 403 + cf-mitigated: challenge for all 5 UAs, /backend-api/codex/responses returns 401 (verify/waf-probe.log). B: waf-probe-headers.py gave the identical table (auth+account/originator → 200, auth only → 403 challenge, nothing → 403); waf-sample.py tally full-daemon-headers 10/10 200, authorization-only 9/10 403 (report had 7/10; consistent 'coin flip'). C: live-probe-1587.ts via pnpm exec tsx → 8/8 OK text='...'. D: started my dev instance (server :23860, daemon :31860) with NODE_OPTIONS preload; system/config voiceTranscriptionEnabled:true; baseline CLI run printed '...' exit 0; challenge run printed exactly 'Error: HTTP 502: Codex transcription request failed with HTTP 403: <html> <head> <meta name="viewport" ...' exit=1, preload log shows 2 daemon fetches (original + cookie retry carrying the simulated __cf_bm), daemon log errorCode codex_request_failed, server log 'Voice transcription failed {attempts:1,maxAttempts:2}'; removing the flag file restored transcription. E: vitest test → 1 passed, 1 failed at line 130 with expected 'codex_request_failed' to be 'codex_service_unavailable'. Root-cause code excerpts (CHATGPT_TRANSCRIBE_URL L28, createChatGptHeaders, fetchChatGpt single cookie retry L352-370, codexRequestErrorCode L384-395 mapping 403 → codex_request_failed, createCodexHttpError appending HTML, server isTransientInferenceError L129-138, voice-transcription fallbackModel: transcriptionModel L148, online-rpc.ts:99 wrapping as ApiError 502) all confirmed at 16ceb3a54. Caveat: I had to edit the hardcoded worktree path/ports/flag paths in run-cli-transcribe.sh and cf-challenge-preload.mjs (copies under verify/) to run step D; the report only mentions editing ports. Dev instance stopped.

findings.problem: run-cli-transcribe.sh and cf-challenge-preload.mjs are hardcoded to the author's environment: WORKTREE=/home/sawyer/projects/bb/.claude/worktrees/wf_242c3e11-a10-20, ports 24862/32862, and the flag/log paths under repro/. The report says only 'edit it for your ports'; a reader following literally gets 'Cannot find module .../wf_242c3e11-a10-20/packages/scripts/dist/commands/run-cli.js'. The wrapper also rm -f's repro/cf-challenge-preload.log (an artifact) on every run.
findings.evidence: repro/run-cli-transcribe.sh lines 7-9; preload FLAG/LOG constants; I had to sed both files into verify/ copies to run step D.
findings.fix: Parameterize WORKTREE/ports via env (e.g. eval "$(scripts/bb-dev-app env)") or state explicitly that WORKTREE, BB_SERVER_URL, BB_HOST_DAEMON_PORT and the preload paths must be edited; write the preload log to a fresh location instead of deleting the artifact.

findings.problem: Report says baseline 'Expected and actual: {"text":"..."}' but the wrapper does not pass --json, so the CLI prints '...' (the appendix command uses --json, the wrapper does not).
findings.fix: Either add --json to the wrapper or state expected output as '...'.

findings.problem: Report calls the simulated output 'the exact CLI error the reporter sees' / 'the reporter's error', but the issue body never quotes an error string (only 'fails with HTTP 403 due to cloudflare'); the exact wording is inferred from code, not observed from the reporter.
findings.evidence: gh issue view 1587: body has no error text; comment is only 'same here'.
findings.fix: Phrase as 'the error the code produces on a challenged network' and note the issue does not quote it.

findings.problem: 'WAF' is used in step A/B without expansion, and 'bot score'/'TLS fingerprint' are asserted as the reason for the reporters' failures without being marked as inference in the TL;DR (they are marked in the confidence line and caveats).
findings.evidence: Step A text: 'A request that passes the WAF...'.
findings.fix: Expand WAF once (web application firewall) and add 'inferred, not observed' next to the per-network explanation in the TL;DR.
